/repos/jdx/demo/pulls/15327.body:
## Summary

A machine that selects several environments had to list every one in `env`, and a script had to recompute that list whenever a role gained a module. A shared `miserc.toml` can now name sets of environments, and `env`, `MISE_ENV` and `-E` accept the names.

```toml
# miserc.toml, in git
[env_sets]
server = ["server", "ssh", "pac"]
workstation = ["workstation", "ssh", "pac", "raycast"]
```

```toml
# ~/.config/mise/miserc.local.toml, on this machine
env = ["workstation"]
```

This machine loads `workstation`, `ssh`, `pac` and `raycast`, and the `mise_env` template variable holds that list. `mise -E workstation` and `MISE_ENV=workstation` expand the same way, and a name that is not a set is still an environment.

`mise bootstrap --save-env` writes the environments given with `-E` or `MISE_ENV` to `miserc.local.toml`, keeping the file's other keys, so a new machine runs `mise bootstrap --from <url> -E workstation --save-env` and later `mise bootstrap --update` runs select the same sets. There is no prompt.

## Rules

- A set expands one level; a set cannot contain another set, and a set may list an environment of its own name.
- Expansion keeps the order a set lists, and an environment listed twice keeps its first position.
- Sets from several miserc files merge per name, closest first. A project `.miserc.toml` loads without trust, so it cannot redefine a set of the system or global `miserc.toml`, as it cannot drop their `env`.
- Members with a path separator are dropped, as for `env`.

Closes https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15316

nodes.title: feat(config): name sets of environments with env_sets in miserc.toml
nodes.body:
## Summary

A machine that selects several environments had to list every one in `env`, and a script had to recompute that list whenever a role gained a module. A shared `miserc.toml` can now name sets of environments, and `env`, `MISE_ENV` and `-E` accept the names.

```toml
# miserc.toml, in git
[env_sets]
server = ["server", "ssh", "pac"]
workstation = ["workstation", "ssh", "pac", "raycast"]
```

```toml
# ~/.config/mise/miserc.local.toml, on this machine
env = ["workstation"]
```

This machine loads `workstation`, `ssh`, `pac` and `raycast`, and the `mise_env` template variable holds that list. `mise -E workstation` and `MISE_ENV=workstation` expand the same way, and a name that is not a set is still an environment.

`mise bootstrap --save-env` writes the environments given with `-E` or `MISE_ENV` to `miserc.local.toml`, keeping the file's other keys, so a new machine runs `mise bootstrap --from <url> -E workstation --save-env` and later `mise bootstrap --update` runs select the same sets. There is no prompt.

## Rules

- A set expands one level; a set cannot contain another set, and a set may list an environment of its own name.
- Expansion keeps the order a set lists, and an environment listed twice keeps its first position.
- Sets from several miserc files merge per name, closest first. A project `.miserc.toml` loads without trust, so it cannot redefine a set of the system or global `miserc.toml`, as it cannot drop their `env`.
- Members with a path separator are dropped, as for `env`.

Closes https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15316

nodes.body:
[P1] [security] **Projects can disable global settings**

An untrusted project can remove a globally selected environment by defining a set with the same name. For example, global `env = ["floor"]` plus project `[env_sets] floor = []` passes this filter because `global_sets` contains only globally defined sets. Expansion then removes `floor`, so `config.floor.toml` no longer loads. This can disable an operator's `paranoid` settings. Protect globally selected plain environments from project-defined sets, not just existing set names.

**How this was verified:** Project set names are filtered only against global set keys, while expansion replaces globally selected environment names with the surviving project set members.

**Knowledge Base Used:** [Configuration loading and trust](https://app.greptile.com/-/switch-tenant?tenant=jdx-org&next=%2Fcustom-context%2Fknowledge-base%2Fjdx%2Fmise%2F-%2Fdocs%2Fconfiguration-loading-and-trust.md)

[P1] **Empty selection loads defaults**

`MISE_ENV=''` now falls back to the default environments in `miserc.toml` instead of selecting none. Previously, a present but empty variable produced `Some(vec![])` and skipped that fallback. With `env = ["production"]`, a caller using `MISE_ENV='' mise …` now loads production config unexpectedly. Keep the distinction between an absent selection and an explicitly empty one when extracting `explicit_environment`.

### Project sets can drop global envs **High Severity** A project `.miserc.toml` is only blocked from redefining set names that the system or global files already defined. `keep_global_envs` then runs on unexpanded names, and `expand_env_sets` later substitutes any remaining project set whose name matches a global `env` entry. That can drop or reorder operator-selected environments, including ones that load a global `paranoid` fragment.
Additional Locations (2) - `src/config/miserc.rs#L107-L127` - `src/env.rs#L263-L270`
Triggered by learned rule: Project miserc cannot drop global environments Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit b34f4b287c32a8837500c009302c64a43b027886. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

**Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Remove `env_sets` from the `mise.toml` settings schema.**

Expansion of set names reads only the miserc files (`src/config/miserc.rs:108-109`). `find_miserc_files` does not collect `mise.toml`. A `[settings.env_sets]` table in `mise.toml` therefore has no effect, but the generated schema accepts it. Users who write the table get no expansion and no error. For example, `-E qa` does not load the environments listed in that set.

The schema is generated. Change `properties()` in `crates/mise-config/src/schema/settings.rs`. It builds the settings object from every leaf setting, and `rc` is not checked there. Exclude this key in the generator. Do not filter on `rc`, because `env_conf_d` is also `rc` and is valid in `mise.toml`.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>
<dl>
<dd>

```diff
 pub(crate) fn properties(settings: &toml::Table) -> Map<String, Value> {
-    group(settings, "")
+    group(settings, "")
+        .into_iter()
+        .filter(|(key, _)| key != "env_sets")
+        .collect()
 }
```

</dd>
</dl>
</details>

Make the `mise.toml` parser reject the same key in the same change, so the schema and the parser agree. Then run `mise run render:schema` to regenerate `schema/mise.json`.

`schema_matches_parser` does not cover this key, so it will not report a mismatch here. Add a `# schema: invalid` example that contains `[settings.env_sets]` if the key must stay covered by the test.

<details>
<summary>Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

